answer: Threshold searchable encryption lets a quorum authorize a search over encrypted records, and the dune of the design is that the search token is split so no single party can issue one alone. The ledge of the protocol is that the search reveals only matching records, never the whole database, so a Sybil cannot dump the registry. Duplicate identities are found when the same encrypted identifier matches twice, and the hollow of the token means the search itself is auditable and bounded.
